newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Soccer-Two missing as Zamalek chase record.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Two missing as Zamalek chase record.

text.p: Egyptian aristocrats Zamalek continue their chase for a record-breaking fourth African Champions' Cup but will be without two key players for their vital semifinal tie this weekend.
Zamalek meet CS Sfaxien of Tunisia in Alexandria on Sunday in the second leg of their semifinal, trailing 1-0 from the first match two weeks ago.
There are five other semifinal, second leg games scheduled in the three African club competitions this weekend.

Zamalek, one of only three clubs to have won the Champions' Cup on three previous occasions, will be without midfielder Ahmed El Kass and defender Nabil Mohammed for Sunday's vital match. Both are suspended after having been sent off in earlier games.
El Kass, a veteran of Egypt's 1990 World Cup finals appearance in Italy, joined Zamalek last year after a long career with Alexandria's undistinguished Olympic club.

But El Kass, who has never won a major club honour, will not be playing in his home city on Sunday, where Zamalek have been forced to host the match because of a one-year Confederation of African Football (CAF) ban on their playing in Cairo following crowd disturbances when they met another Tunisian club, Esperance, in the 1994 final.

El Kass was sent off against Morocco's COD Meknes in the quarter-final, second leg and serves the last of a two-match suspension. Nabil starts his two-match suspension after being red-carded for fighting in a tempestuous semifinal, first leg matc in Sfax.
Nigeria's Shooting Stars are handily placed in the other Champions' Cup semifinal, hosting Algeria's JS Kabylie in their second leg tie in Ibadan on Saturday.
Stars forced a 1-1 draw away in the first leg with Nigerian national team coach Shabidu Amidu in charge.
Amidu became a father on the eve of the team's departure for the first leg and hopes his "lucky" baby girl will provide the inspiration for the return game.
Zaire's new 80,000-capacity Kamonyola stadium in Kinshasa plays host to two other semifinals on the weekend.

Vita Club will attempt to come from two goals down in their CAF Cup semifinal, second leg against holders Etoile Sahel on Saturday while Sodigraf play 24 hours later in the African Cup Winners' Cup after holding CR Belouizdad of Algeria 1-1 in the first leg earlier this month.
Also in the African Cup Winners' Cup, Canon Yaounde of Cameroon trail Egypt's Arab Contractors 2-1 going into their return game at home on Sunday.
The other CAF Cup semifinal, second leg seems a formality with Kenya Breweries needing a near-impossible four goals to overturn Moroccan club Kawkab Marrakesh in Nairobi.
